systems.*.info.hostname: Plain identification the agent hands over verbatim — the string IS the whole content.
systems.*.info.os: The value is the platform family itself: Linux, macOS, Windows or FreeBSD.
systems.*.info.kernel: Plain identification the agent hands over verbatim — the string IS the whole content.
systems.*.info.cpu_model: Plain identification the agent hands over verbatim — the string IS the whole content.
systems.*.info.arch: Plain identification the agent hands over verbatim — the string IS the whole content.
systems.*.info.agent_version: Plain identification the agent hands over verbatim — the string IS the whole content.
systems.*.info.cores: A plain count of what the name says; there is no unit to get wrong.
systems.*.info.threads: A plain count of what the name says; there is no unit to get wrong.
systems.*.info.uptime: The name and the second unit are the whole statement.
systems.*.info.uptime_text: The same uptime written out for reading, and the name says so.
systems.*.cpu.usage: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all.
systems.*.cpu.user: Names its own half of the CPU split; only the odd members (iowait, steal) carry an explanation.
systems.*.cpu.system: Names its own half of the CPU split; only the odd members (iowait, steal) carry an explanation.
systems.*.cpu.idle: The plain complement of the busy shares, in percent.
systems.*.cpu.cores.*: The same CPU reading once per core; the name carries the core index.
systems.*.memory.percent: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike buffers and ZFS ARC, which do carry one.
systems.*.memory.used: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike buffers and ZFS ARC, which do carry one.
systems.*.memory.total: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike buffers and ZFS ARC, which do carry one.
systems.*.memory.swap_used: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike buffers and ZFS ARC, which do carry one.
systems.*.memory.swap_total: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike buffers and ZFS ARC, which do carry one.
systems.*.network.sent: A rate whose name and MB/s unit say it all — unlike the cumulative totals, which do carry one.
systems.*.network.recv: A rate whose name and MB/s unit say it all — unlike the cumulative totals, which do carry one.
systems.*.network.interfaces.*.up: The same rate once per interface; the channel carries the interface name.
systems.*.network.interfaces.*.down: The same rate once per interface; the channel carries the interface name.
systems.*.filesystems.*.disk_percent: The same disk reading once per mount point; the channel carries the mount point.
systems.*.filesystems.*.disk_used: The same disk reading once per mount point; the channel carries the mount point.
systems.*.filesystems.*.disk_total: The same disk reading once per mount point; the channel carries the mount point.
systems.*.filesystems.*.read_speed: The same disk reading once per mount point; the channel carries the mount point.
systems.*.filesystems.*.write_speed: The same disk reading once per mount point; the channel carries the mount point.
systems.*.zfs.*.disk_percent: The same disk reading once per pool; the channel carries the pool name as zpool lists it.
systems.*.zfs.*.disk_used: The same disk reading once per pool; the channel carries the pool name as zpool lists it.
systems.*.zfs.*.disk_total: The same disk reading once per pool; the channel carries the pool name as zpool lists it.
systems.*.zfs.*.read_speed: The same disk reading once per pool; the channel carries the pool name as zpool lists it.
systems.*.zfs.*.write_speed: The same disk reading once per pool; the channel carries the pool name as zpool lists it.
systems.*.zfs.*.vdevs.*.state: The vdev's ZFS health word; common.states lists every word it can take.
systems.*.zfs.*.datasets.*.used: The same dataset reading once per dataset; the channel carries the dataset name.
systems.*.zfs.*.datasets.*.avail: The same dataset reading once per dataset; the channel carries the dataset name.
systems.*.zfs.*.datasets.*.mountpoint: Plain identification the agent hands over verbatim — the path IS the whole content.
systems.*.gpu.*.usage: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike the package power, which does carry one.
systems.*.gpu.*.memory_used: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike the package power, which does carry one.
systems.*.gpu.*.memory_total: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike the package power, which does carry one.
systems.*.gpu.*.power: Power draw in watts — name, role and unit leave nothing open.
systems.*.gpu.*.engines.*: One engine's load in percent; the name is the driver's own word for that engine.
systems.*.temperature.sensors.*: The name is the sensor's own identifier from the agent — a sentence about it would describe the machine, not this adapter.
systems.*.fans.*: The name is the fan's own hwmon identifier from the agent; rpm says the rest.
systems.*.battery.batteries.*: The name is the battery's own identifier from the agent; the percent unit says the rest.
systems.*.battery.percent: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike charging, which does carry one.
systems.*.containers.*.status: Docker's own status line, which already reads as a sentence ("Up 3 hours").
systems.*.containers.*.image: Plain identification the agent hands over verbatim — the image reference IS the whole content.
systems.*.containers.*.memory: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike the network volume, which does carry one.
systems.*.services.*.state: The systemd state word itself; common.states lists every word it can take — unlike the sub-state, which does carry an explanation.
systems.*.services.*.memory: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all — unlike the peak values, which do carry one.
systems.*.smart.*.model: Plain identification smartctl hands over verbatim — the string IS the whole content.
systems.*.smart.*.serial: Plain identification smartctl hands over verbatim — the string IS the whole content.
systems.*.smart.*.firmware: Plain identification smartctl hands over verbatim — the string IS the whole content.
systems.*.smart.*.interface: The bus the drive sits on, as smartctl names it (sata, nvme, scsi).
systems.*.smart.*.capacity: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all.
systems.*.smart.*.temperature: A reading whose name, role and unit say it all.
